hypothesis: A buried normal fault is a step in the GP-1012-calibrated inverted basement surface; the step fixes where to look, and an out-of-fold habitat model over 28 catalogue-independent features (the 19 supplied bands plus the lane's own inverted depth, depth gradient, step throw, step indicator, corridor indicator, basin indicator and Euler SI=0 source depth) fixes where to put the dot.
mechanism: Basement throw under alluvium -> isostatic-residual gradient maximum (200 m Parker/Oldenburg slab inversion, GP-1012-calibrated, Blakely-Simpson maxima, measured throw >= 80 m) -> the same gravity products enter a logistic habitat model trained on the visible mapped faults -> 40,000 binary dots at 3 px spacing, every dot more than 3 px from a mapped trace.
named_non_fault_mimic: Density contrasts inside the basement (intrabasement lithologic contacts) produce the same isostatic-residual gradient maximum. The lane's discriminator is implemented, not asserted: the inverted depth (a basin step sits on thick low-density fill) and the Euler SI=0 source depth (a basement edge is shallow, an intrabasement contact is deep). Measured logistic weights: inv_depth -0.172, inv_depth_hgm -0.204, euler_depth -0.053, step_throw -0.046, step_indicator -0.006, corridor_indicator +0.194 -- i.e. the lane's instruments are in the model and carry almost no marginal information, which is the honest negative result for the lane's premise.

leakage_canary.finding: IR-61-LEAK-01: the gradient-boosted habitat model's out-of-fold canary AUC was 0.901, above the 0.90 line. The leave-one-quadrant-out retest shows why: with no training pixel inside the scored quadrant its AUC falls to 0.518-0.618 and its pooled DTI to the random baseline. The 0.901 was adjacency to the visible traces the model memorised, not skill. The shipped file therefore uses the L2 logistic model, whose canary AUC is 0.626 with no caveat.
